problem: Existing VLN surveys organize the literature by timeline, model paradigm, or benchmark, and pay little attention to the internal components of VLN systems and how those components are functionally coupled.
motivation: VLN has grown from discrete simulated path-following into continuous control, interactive clarification, open-vocabulary perception and real-robot deployment. A component-level view (instruction, environment representation, embodied agent) is needed to understand how internal capabilities evolve and to guide system design and deployment.
key_idea: Survey VLN as a navigation system made of instruction, environment-representation and embodied-agent components, and organize the literature around their functions and interactions.
insight: Framing VLN by component interactions (instruction understanding and action generation, instruction–environment alignment, robot–environment interaction understanding) exposes the coupling that timeline- or benchmark-based surveys hide. The abstract identifies four trends toward open-world deployment: reasoning-enhanced planning, open-vocabulary and online semantic mapping, long-horizon memory with structured spatial representation, and sim-to-real transfer across platforms. Only the abstract was available, so no ablation or empirical evidence can be cited.
method: Task, dataset and evaluation summary: covers VLN task definitions, datasets and evaluation settings.
Instruction understanding and action generation: reviews representative methods for parsing instructions and producing actions.
Instruction–environment alignment: reviews grounding of language to environment representations.
Robot–environment interaction understanding: reviews how embodied agents interact with and understand the environment.

Trends toward open-world and real-world deployment: reasoning-enhanced planning, open-vocabulary and online semantic mapping, long-horizon memory and structured spatial representation, sim-to-real transfer.
numbers_note: abstract only; survey with no experimental results
results: This is a survey, so it reports no experimental results. It offers a component-centric analytical framework and a discussion of trends in VLN moving toward open-world and real-world deployment.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so the coverage and depth of the review cannot be assessed.
As a survey, it provides no new empirical evaluation or unified benchmark comparison.
compares_to: Prior VLN surveys organized by timeline, model paradigm, or benchmark
